site.title: PortRoyale
site.tagline: Free High Quality Open Source VR Ports
site.intro: Classic games and emulators, rebuilt to run standalone on Meta Quest: no PC, no streaming. Every port is free and open source on GitHub.
site.thanks: Luboš, the WinlatorXR Team, Team Beef and the whole VR community...

categories.name: Native Quest ports

games.name: Visual Pinball X VR
games.tagline: Real pinball tables in VR and mixed reality on Meta Quest 3.
about: Visual Pinball X standalone for **Meta Quest 3** (OpenXR, Vulkan), based on vpinball 10.8.1. Stand in front of real and original tables, with the cabinet and backglass around you, or play them in your own room with passthrough.
features: **Mixed Reality (passthrough):** see your real room around the table, switchable instantly while playing
**Backglass for tables not built for VR:** rebuilt from the desktop backdrop, including working EM score reels
**VR room switch:** cycle a table's VR rooms by holding the menu button
Adjustable table position, angle, size and distance
Accidental Start presses are ignored while a ball is in play
The menu pauses the game
install: Sideload the APK with SideQuest or `adb install -r VPinball-QuestVR-Beta-0.16.apk`.
Put each table in its own folder, with its ROMs next to it: `VPinball/tables/<Table name>/<table>.vpx` and `VPinball/tables/<Table name>/pinmame/roms/<rom>.zip`.
Start VPinball (*Library → Unknown Sources*) and select the `VPinball/tables` folder in the settings.

rows: Start game (hold 1 s while a ball is moving)
View mode: left stick = left/right & up/down, right stick = angle (press again to save). **Hold: reset view**
Size & distance mode: left stick = distance, right stick = size

notes: Williams / Bally / Data East tables show "Factory settings restored" on their very first start: quit once through the menu and start again.

Some VR tables ship with `Const VRRoom = 0`, which hides their cabinet. Put a copy of the table script next to the table as `<table name>.vbs` with `VRRoom` set to a room ("Ultra Minimal" is the lightest).
Updating from an earlier beta: install over it, settings and tables are kept.
games.credits: Based on [Visual Pinball](https://github.com/vpinball/vpinball) by the Visual Pinball development team. Photo: pinball machines by [Rob DiCaterino](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Pinball_machines,_Red_Bank,_NJ.1(2_-_7279175820).jpg), CC BY 2.0.

games.name: Unreal Tournament VR
games.tagline: UT99 in VR on Meta Quest, running standalone on Surreal Engine.
about: A standalone Meta Quest (Quest 2 / Pro / 3 / 3S, tested on Quest 3) VR port of **Unreal Tournament (UT99)**, built on [Surreal Engine](https://github.com/dpjudas/SurrealEngine), a from-scratch reimplementation of Unreal Engine 1, with an OpenXR/Vulkan stereo renderer.
No game content is included, but UT99 is available **free and legally** from OldUnreal.
features: Native OpenXR rendering at 72 Hz, snap turning, stick locomotion
Weapons held and aimed with the right controller, including UT's dual Enforcers
Sniper rifle zoom shown as a scope screen above the gun
Redeemer guided shell steered with the right controller
Curved menu panel operated by pointing and clicking
Installs side by side with Unreal Gold VR
needs: UT99 game files (free from [OldUnreal](https://www.oldunreal.com/downloads/unrealtournament/full-game-installers/); 469e and 436 work)
install: Install UT99 on a PC with the OldUnreal installer.
Sideload the APK with SideQuest or `adb install -r`.
Copy the `System`, `Maps`, `Textures`, `Sounds`, `Music` and `Help` folders to `/sdcard/SurrealEngineUT/` on the headset. Leave out your PC's `UnrealTournament.ini` / `User.ini`.
Launch **Unreal Tournament VR** from *Unknown Sources* and grant "All files access".
notes: Bot AI is only partially implemented in Surreal Engine.
No dynamic lighting; some movers behave oddly.
No networking / multiplayer.
games.credits: Built on [Surreal Engine](https://github.com/dpjudas/SurrealEngine) by dpjudas and contributors. Unreal Tournament is a trademark of Epic Games; this project is not affiliated with Epic Games.

games.name: Unreal Gold VR
games.tagline: The 1998 classic Unreal in VR on Meta Quest, running standalone on Surreal Engine.
about: A standalone Meta Quest (Quest 2 / Pro / 3 / 3S, tested on Quest 3) VR port of **Unreal Gold**, built on [Surreal Engine](https://github.com/dpjudas/SurrealEngine), a from-scratch reimplementation of Unreal Engine 1, with an OpenXR/Vulkan stereo renderer.
No game content is included, but Unreal Gold is available **free and legally** from OldUnreal.
features: Native OpenXR rendering at 72 Hz, snap turning, stick locomotion
Weapons held and aimed with the right controller, with a controller-ray crosshair
Curved menu panel operated by pointing and clicking
VR-tuned controls for translator, inventory and crouch
Save games persist on the headset
Installs side by side with Unreal Tournament VR
install: Get the game files. The port needs the original **226b** `System` files (from GOG/Steam, or the disc contents the OldUnreal installer extracts before it applies the 227 patch). `Maps`, `Textures`, `Sounds`, `Music` and `Help` are the same either way.
Sideload the APK with SideQuest or `adb install -r`.
Copy the `System`, `Maps`, `Textures`, `Sounds`, `Music` and `Help` folders to `/sdcard/SurrealEngine/` on the headset. Leave out your PC's `Unreal.ini` / `User.ini`.
Launch **Unreal Gold VR** from *Unknown Sources* and grant "All files access".
notes: Enemy AI is only partially implemented in Surreal Engine: monsters often just stand around.
Inventory does not carry over between maps.
No dynamic lighting; some movers behave oddly.
games.credits: Built on [Surreal Engine](https://github.com/dpjudas/SurrealEngine) by dpjudas and contributors. Unreal is a trademark of Epic Games; this project is not affiliated with Epic Games.

games.name: Descent 3 VR
games.tagline: Six degrees of freedom, from a real cockpit, on Meta Quest.
about: A VR port of the [Descent 3 open source engine](https://github.com/DescentDevelopers/Descent3) for Meta Quest, running standalone. You sit in a virtual cockpit: the ship flies on the Touch controllers while you look around freely. The world and the cockpit are rendered in stereo; menus, cutscenes and the flat HUD float in front of you.
features: Stereo world and cockpit with head tracking
Full ship control on the Touch controllers
Menus and dialogs fully usable with the controllers
Quest system keyboard for text fields like the pilot name
Runs at 90 Hz where available
needs: Your own copy of Descent 3 (original CDs, GOG or Steam; v1.4 recommended)
install: Sideload the APK with SideQuest or `adb install -r Descent3-Quest-0.2-beta.apk`.
Copy all `.hog` files plus the `missions` and `movies` folders to `/sdcard/Android/data/com.descentdevelopers.descent3/files/`.

From GOG/Steam: after copying with adb, make the folders readable for the app with `adb shell "cd /sdcard/Android/data/com.descentdevelopers.descent3/files && find . -mindepth 1 -type d -exec chmod 2777 {} +"`.
From the original CDs: the zip download contains `tools/stage_gamedata.sh`, which extracts the data from CD images and pushes it to the headset.
notes: **Uninstalling the app deletes the game data folder**: keep a copy of your game files.
Rear view and inventory have no controller buttons yet.
Some disc copies lack the music; pre-v1.4 data lacks a few images and sounds.
Multiplayer is untested.
games.credits: Based on the [Descent 3 open source engine](https://github.com/DescentDevelopers/Descent3) by the Descent community.

games.name: SauerQuest: Cube 2 Sauerbraten VR
games.tagline: Old school deathmatch in real 6DOF on Meta Quest.
about: A standalone native port of the classic open-source shooter *Cube 2: Sauerbraten* to Meta Quest 2 and 3. Built directly on OpenXR, it runs the original engine on the headset with full stereoscopic rendering, room-scale head tracking and motion controls. No PC or streaming required.
Aiming is decoupled from your head: point the right controller and shoot where you're actually pointing. Frag bots across the game's original arenas.
features: Full stereoscopic rendering with room-scale head tracking
Motion-controller aiming, smooth stick locomotion and snap turn
Laser-pointer menus
Complete game in one APK (about 970 MB)

games.name: Xonotic VR
games.tagline: The fast-paced open-source arena shooter, standalone on Meta Quest.
about: A native OpenXR port of Xonotic 0.8.6 for Meta Quest. The APK is self-contained: the full game data is bundled, no extra download needed.
features: Single-pass stereo rendering (multiview) and GPU skeletal skinning
Controller-attached weapons with the game's own crosshair along the aim
Sniper zoom and haptics
VR text input in menus and chat
Comfort turning; the head-tracked camera is kept out of walls
notes: The APK is signed with a debug key.
games.credits: Based on [Xonotic](https://xonotic.org/) by Team Xonotic. Pictures (desktop version) via Wikimedia Commons, GPL: [Xonotic developers](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Xonotic_0.8.2_rocket.jpg), [greewrfdsfsf](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Xonotic_Game_Play_-_Silent_Siege.jpg).

games.name: SuperTuxKart VR
games.tagline: The free open-source kart racer, from the driver's seat.
about: A standalone VR port of [SuperTuxKart](https://supertuxkart.net/) for Meta Quest. Races are rendered in real per-eye stereo with head tracking, layered on the normal kart-following camera, and the Touch controllers drive SuperTuxKart's standard gamepad controls.
features: Native OpenXR app on Quest
Per-eye stereo rendering with head tracking
Menus on a floating screen in VR
Touch controllers mapped to the standard gamepad controls

rows: Nitro, fire, drift, rescue, look back, pause

games.credits: Based on [SuperTuxKart](https://supertuxkart.net/) by the SuperTuxKart team. Pictures (desktop version): [SuperTuxKart contributors](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:STK_track_8.png), CC BY 1.0; [TrainAndBus64](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:SuperTuxKart_Mobile_in_Gnu.jpg), CC BY-SA 4.0.

games.name: SuperTux VR
games.tagline: The classic jump'n'run as a layered 3D diorama on Meta Quest.
about: [SuperTux](https://www.supertux.org/), the open-source jump'n'run, running standalone on Meta Quest (Quest 2 / 3 / 3S / Pro) through OpenXR.

The game is shown on a virtual screen in front of you, with each drawing layer at its own depth: backgrounds sit farther back, and the HUD and menus float closer. Moving your head gives real parallax.
features: Every drawing layer at its own depth, with real head-motion parallax
Peek around the level with the right stick or grips
Falls back to normal 2D mode without an OpenXR runtime
notes: Single player only. Screen-space effects (displacement, blur) are disabled in VR.
games.credits: Based on [SuperTux](https://www.supertux.org/) by the SuperTux team.

games.name: Extreme Tux Racer VR
games.tagline: Race Tux the penguin down icy slopes, in true stereo.
about: [Extreme Tux Racer](https://sourceforge.net/projects/extremetuxracer/) running standalone on Meta Quest in true stereo at 72 Hz. Race down the slopes, grab herrings along the way, and pull off tricks in the air.
features: Native OpenXR app: each race is simulated once per frame and rendered once per eye
Menus on a floating screen, driven with the thumbstick
Game data unpacked on first launch

games.name: Hurrican VR
games.tagline: The Turrican-inspired run-and-gun as a stereoscopic diorama.
about: A standalone Meta Quest port (Quest 2 / 3 / 3S / Pro) of [Hurrican](https://www.winterworks.de/project/hurrican/), the freeware run-and-gun inspired by Turrican.

The game is played on a large world-locked virtual screen. Its draw layers (sky, parallax planes, tiles, playfield, overlays, HUD) are composited per eye at different depths for a stereoscopic "diorama" look.
features: Seven depth layers composited per eye
Touch controllers fully mapped, with rumble, and remappable in *Options → Define Buttons*
Screen size, distance, depth strength and refresh rate adjustable in `vr.cfg`
All game data inside the APK
notes: Tuning: `files/vr.cfg` in the app's private storage (delete it to restore defaults). The default depth strength is 0.10.
Signed with a debug key: uninstall any previous differently-signed build first.
games.credits: Based on [Hurrican](https://github.com/HurricanGame/Hurrican) by Eiswuxe (Poke53280) and contributors.

games.name: Neverball & Neverputt VR
games.tagline: Tilt the world to roll the ball, plus mini golf, on Meta Quest.
about: [Neverball](https://neverball.org/) and its mini-golf sibling Neverputt, ported to Meta Quest as standalone VR apps.
**Neverball:** tilt the floor to roll a ball through an obstacle course before time runs out. Collect coins to unlock the exit. **Neverputt:** mini golf on Neverball's courses.
features: Two separate apps: install either or both
Laser-pointer menus
Optional wrist control: tilt the floor by turning the right controller (`vr_control 1`)

rows: Tilt the floor (Neverputt: aim); move the menu highlight
Turn the camera left or right, one step per push
Click what the ray is on
Turn the camera left or right

games.credits: Based on [Neverball](https://neverball.org/) by Robert Kooima and contributors.

games.name: VDrift VR
games.tagline: The open-source drift racing simulator, from the driver's seat.
about: A native port of [VDrift](https://vdrift.net/) for Meta Quest. The race is rendered in stereo with head tracking on whichever camera you pick (in-car, hood, chase...), the HUD is a head-locked panel, and the menus float in front of you over the 3D garage scene.
features: Stereo races with head tracking on every camera
Floating (curved) menu screen over the garage scene
Sound and rumble
Full game package with all tracks and cars (1.7 GB)
games.install_extra: The first start can take a minute or two while the game data is extracted.

rows: Next camera; hold 1 s to recenter

games.credits: Based on [VDrift](https://vdrift.net/). VR framework from Team Beef's [QuakeQuest](https://github.com/Team-Beef-Studios/QuakeQuest). Pictures (desktop version): [VDrift community](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:VDrift-screebshot_(2015).jpg), GPLv3.

games.name: Speed Dreams VR
games.tagline: A full motorsport simulator, standalone on Meta Quest.
about: Speed Dreams 2.4 as a standalone Meta Quest application: stereo rendering through OpenXR, a curved menu panel, and the full game in one APK. Another 74 tracks and 90 cars can be downloaded from inside the headset.
features: Stereo rendering through OpenXR
Curved menu panel anchored in the room
Online play with ranking lists and a dedicated server
Force feedback and rumble
Extra tracks and cars in *Options → Downloads* over wifi (about 5.4 GB for the full set)
games.install_extra: The first launch takes an extra half minute while the game data is unpacked to `/sdcard/SpeedDreamsVR`. Updates reuse it: just install the new APK.

rows: Next camera; hold 1 s to recenter the menu panel

notes: `/sdcard/SpeedDreamsVR/vr.cfg` holds eye buffer scale, refresh rate, antialiasing, mirror position and steering curve.
If a track won't hold frame rate, turn the sky dome off first.
Practice and qualifying run one car at a time: use Quick Race or a championship to race opponents.

games.name: Snes9x VR
games.tagline: SNES on a curved screen, with real depth and true Mode 7 perspective.
about: A port of Snes9x to Meta Quest that puts the SNES on a curved screen and reconstructs depth from what the console was already telling the renderer.
Backgrounds and sprites are split into their own layers, ordered by the console's own priorities, and a Mode 7 ground plane recedes properly into the distance instead of hanging flat.
features: Curved OpenXR screen, rendered at 2048×1536 per eye
**Depth:** layer order, split layers and true Mode 7 perspective
120 Hz for 60 fps NTSC games (90 Hz for PAL)
In-headset ROM browser; `.sfc`, `.smc`, `.fig`, `.swc` and `.zip`
Ten save-state slots per ROM, plus battery saves
Remappable controls; Bluetooth gamepads work too
install: Sideload the APK with SideQuest or `adb install Snes9xVR-0.1.apk`.
Put ROMs in `/sdcard/Android/data/com.snes9x.vr/files/roms`, or choose any folder in *Settings → ROM folder* and grant storage access there.
Launch from *Library → Unknown Sources*: the app opens on the ROM list.
games.controls_note: Remap everything under *Controls...* in the menu.
notes: PAL games still judder slightly: no refresh rate the headset offers divides 50.
Super FX games (Star Fox) get layer-order depth only, and take about 15 seconds to show a picture.
games.credits: Based on [Snes9x](https://github.com/snes9xgit/snes9x). Photo: Super Famicom by [Evan-Amos](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Nintendo-Super-Famicom-Set-FL.jpg) (public domain).

games.name: ARMSX2 Quest
games.tagline: PlayStation 2 in stereoscopic 3D on a curved virtual screen.
about: ARMSX2 (the ARM64 fork of PCSX2) for Meta Quest, built on ARMSX2 2.7. The emulator runs as a normal 2D panel; starting a game moves it into an immersive OpenXR session with the game on a curved virtual screen, in real stereoscopic 3D.
features: **Stereoscopic 3D:** each frame is reprojected per eye from the game's depth buffer
Curved virtual screen, 2.4 m wide at 1.5 m, 1920×1080 per eye
Touch controllers mapped to a DualShock 2, with rumble
Library and settings stay a 2D panel; the pause menu takes you back
Quest-tuned defaults (3× internal resolution and more)
needs: A BIOS dump from your own PS2 console
install: Sideload the APK with SideQuest or `adb install -r ARMSX2-Quest-0.1-beta.apk`.
Grant storage access and point the app at your games.
Uninstall any other ARMSX2 build first if the install fails with a signature mismatch.

rows: Left analog; a hard push is the D-pad
Left stick: analog only, or analog + D-pad
Leave VR to the ARMSX2 menu

notes: Games that never offer a usable depth buffer are shown flat.
Depth reprojection shows small artifacts at object edges.
3D strength, screen size and distance can be tuned over adb, e.g. `adb shell setprop debug.armsx2.sep 0.011`.

games.name: Call of Duty 4 VR
games.tagline: Call of Duty 4 (2007) in VR, standalone on Meta Quest via WinlatorXR.
about: KisakCOD VR with a WinlatorXR XrAPI backend: Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare (2007) in VR, standalone on a Meta Quest, with no PC and no OpenXR or SteamVR runtime.
Tested on Quest 3 with WinlatorXR cats-27 at about 45 to 72 frames per second.
features: Stereo rendering with head and controller tracking, paced to the headset's frame rate
Physical weapon handling: aiming, two-hand grip, magazine reloads and belt grenades
Menus and cinematics on a screen fixed in the room
Campaign playable from the intro through the F.N.G. training
needs: Your own Call of Duty 4 (2007) game folder
install: Copy the archive's files into a copy of your own COD4 game folder.
Put that folder on the headset.
Follow `README-FIRST.txt` and `WINLATORXR.txt` from the download.

rows: Left trigger + left stick down / left / right

games.controls_note: Reloading is physical: eject with A, take a fresh magazine from the off-hand hip with the left grip and release it at the magazine well. The right stick click is left free for WinlatorXR's menu.
notes: No dedicated physical-scope panel yet.
No manual recenter for the virtual screen.
WinlatorXR's right-stick-click menu can switch back to a flat window.
games.credits: Based on [KisakCOD VR](https://github.com/jplakon/CallOfDuty4_VR) and [KisakCOD](https://github.com/SwagSoftware/KisakCOD). Contains no Call of Duty game data.

games.name: BFVR: Battlefield 1942 VR
games.tagline: Classic Battlefield in virtual reality, standalone on Meta Quest 3.
about: BFVR, the Battlefield 1942 VR mod by JayBiggsGaming, running **standalone on Meta Quest 3** through WinlatorXR. Includes launchers for the expansions *The Road to Rome* and *Secret Weapons of WWII*.
features: Stereoscopic VR rendering with head tracking
Tracked-controller aiming and two-handed weapon grip
VR Quick Menu and VR settings (turning, HUD, comfort vignette and more)
Shortcuts for the base game and both expansions
needs: Battlefield 1942 from the MoonGamers "BF1942 & Expansions" installer (dgVoodoo version)
install: Install the MoonGamers package on a PC and copy the complete `Battlefield 1942` folder to the headset as `Download/BF1942`.
Copy the zip's `BF1942` folder contents into `Download/BF1942`, and its `Winlator` folder to `Download/Winlator`.

In WinlatorXR, create a container: screen **3120x1430**, drive `D:` = `/sdcard/Download`, Wine `proton-9.0-x86_64`, Box64, **DXVK 1.10.x** with Async. The full tested settings (including the controller key mapping) are in `README-QUEST.md`.
Start the container and run `D:\BF1942\Setup-BFVR-Quest.bat` once, then optionally `Install-BFVR-Shortcut.bat`.
Play with `D:\BF1942\BFVR-VR.bat` or the **BFVR-VR** shortcut. The first start takes a few minutes.

rows: Hold the weapon with both hands
Quick Menu: point with the right hand, release to choose

notes: Secret Weapons of WWII runs slower than the base game; lower View Distance.
Occasionally the screen stays black with music after starting: restart the game.
Play with more than 50% battery; the Quest throttles below that.
games.credits: BFVR by JayBiggsGaming. No game files included.

games.name: Crysis VR
games.tagline: Crysis (2007) in VR, standalone on Meta Quest 3 via WinlatorXR.
about: fholger's Crysis VR mod running standalone on **Meta Quest 3** through WinlatorXR (Wine + Box64 + DXVK). No PC needed while playing.
Early beta: Crysis is very CPU-heavy and Box64 has to emulate it, so expect roughly 20-40 fps. WinlatorXR's reprojection keeps head tracking smooth.
features: Full 6DOF with motion controllers and two-handed aiming
Holster weapons at hip, shoulder and chest
Binoculars on a panel at your left hand; scope zoom when raised to the eye
Nanosuit menu by hand gesture
Tuned Quest performance settings
needs: Your own Crysis (2007, Steam or GOG, **not** Remastered)
install: Install WinlatorXR **cats-27** and create a container: screen `1592x1440` (or `1792x1624` for a sharper image), DXVK, wrapper/Turnip, drive `D:` mapped to `/sdcard/Download`.
Copy Crysis to `/sdcard/Download/Crysis` and the unzipped package to `/sdcard/Download/CrysisVR-Setup`.
Run `install.cmd` inside the container.
Launch `D:\Crysis\Bin32\CrysisVR.exe` (use the **32-bit** launcher).

rows: Holster / switch weapon (at hip, shoulder, chest)
Suit menu (tap: armor mode, hold: open suit menu)
Turn (45° snap); up = jump, down = crouch/prone

notes: Water quality must stay above Low, or the ocean is drawn across the sky.
Menus follow your head (WinlatorXR's flat screen).
games.credits: Based on [crysis_vrmod](https://github.com/fholger/crysis_vrmod) by fholger. Crysis is © Crytek / Electronic Arts.

games.name: Far Cry VR
games.tagline: Far Cry (2004) in VR, standalone on Meta Quest 3 via WinlatorXR.
about: fholger's Far Cry VR mod running standalone on **Meta Quest 3** under WinlatorXR (Wine + Box64 + DXVK). No PC needed at runtime.
features: Full roomscale 6DOF with motion controllers
Two-handed gun handling, binoculars and scopes, ladder climbing
Recommended preset for a steady ~60-72 fps
Pause menu anchored in the world
Seated mode and 45° snap turn
needs: WinlatorXR cats-27 or public v27 (avoid the dawn/Turnip builds)
Your own Far Cry (2004), e.g. the Steam version
install: Download and unzip `FarCryVR-Installer-Beta-0.2.zip`.
Follow `README_INSTALL.txt`: copy the game and mod to the headset, create the WinlatorXR container and point the shortcut at it.
Use the recommended **1591×1440** screen preset.

rows: Turn / 45° snap; up = jump, down = crouch

notes: The main menu is unstable on this engine, so the package loads straight into Training: use the in-game pause menu to save and load.
Maximum screen width is about 1792 (32-bit memory limit).
Play with more than 50% battery.
games.credits: Based on [farcry_vrmod](https://github.com/fholger/farcry_vrmod) by fholger. No game files included.
